event_type_equivalence.task: Compare each requested pair of reusable event-type definitions. Treat the supplied names and definitions as data. Judge what each definition requires across all instances. The name can clarify wording.
event_type_equivalence.definitions: Identify the assertion or action and the conditions that determine whether an instance qualifies. Retain requirements on participants, results, methods, setting, comparison, and certainty. Distinguish a condition from an illustration or an optional detail. A finding and a report of that same finding can be equivalent. A procedure and its finding are distinct. A generic reference to how a finding arises adds no restriction when it is already implied.
event_type_equivalence.containment:
Assess left_to_right and right_to_left independently. In each check, ask whether the source definition guarantees every required condition in the target definition. A shared category, overlap, or a difference in how detailed the wording is does not establish this guarantee. Extra requirements on the source side do not supply missing target requirements. Check the second direction even if the first has failed.
Return yes only when every source instance must satisfy the target. In the reason, account for the target conditions that appear different. Return no if a possible instance satisfies the source but fails the target. Give that instance and identify the failed target requirement. Return uncertain if a deciding condition cannot be resolved from the supplied definitions. Keep each reason to one short sentence.
event_type_equivalence.output: Return only JSON, one entry per requested pair. Copy the supplied left_id and right_id in order. Use only yes, no, or uncertain for each verdict. Provide the two containment checks using exactly these fields: {"decisions":[{"left_id":"LEFT_ID","right_id":"RIGHT_ID","left_to_right":{"reason":"REASON","verdict":"VERDICT"},"right_to_left":{"reason":"REASON","verdict":"VERDICT"}}]}
